name: workmap
description: A live map beside the chat: memory, files, shell, web, model, agents, skills and hooks light up as they are used. Began as lot-map by Aleksei Volodin.

language.title: Language
language.description: The language of the labels on the map.

coreName.title: Name at the centre
coreName.description: What the circle in the middle of the map says, up to ten characters.

memoryServers.title: Memory servers
memoryServers.description: MCP servers whose tools light the Memory station.

memoryCommands.title: Memory commands
memoryCommands.description: Shell commands or scripts that light the Memory station. A name counts when it is the command itself or begins with it and a hyphen, an underscore or a dot.

memorySubcommands.title: Memory subcommands
memorySubcommands.description: Words after a memory command that the map may show, such as add or search. Without them a memory command goes by its own name, because the word after it may be content.

memoryPaths.title: Memory paths
memoryPaths.description: Parts of a path that make a file a memory. Claude Code's own memory folder always counts.

memoryLabels.title: Memory labels
memoryLabels.description: Short names for memory tools, each written as tool=name. A tool without one goes by its own name.

serverStations.title: Servers on a station
serverStations.description: Put an MCP server's tools on a station of the map, each written as server=station. The stations are files, shell, web, browser, agents, skills and you. Memory keeps memoryServers, which wins if a server is in both. A server without an entry, or with an unknown station, goes where the mod puts it.

hookRecords.title: Hooks add numbered records
hookRecords.description: Turn on if a hook of yours adds memory records numbered like [#123]: the map then shows them on the Memory station, by number only. It counts such numbers in the text of any hook, not only a memory one.

hookReasons.title: Show why a hook refused
hookReasons.description: Show the first line of a hook's refusal, up to 72 characters. Off, the map says only which tool was stopped: a refusal may quote what the hook found.

errorReasons.title: Show why a call failed
errorReasons.description: Show the first line with text of a failed call's error, up to 72 characters. Off, the row says only that the call failed: an error may quote what the call touched.

contextCost.title: What each call adds to the context
contextCost.description: Each row says about how many tokens the context grew by with its call's answer, the map adds each station's sum to its count and a pulse's width follows its call's tokens. An estimate: the growth of one model step, which also holds the model's own words, what hooks added and, at the start of a turn, the message, shared among that step's calls. It shows one step late, and a call whose step was the last of a turn gets none.

guardedHooks.title: Hooks a guard skips
guardedHooks.description: Turn off on a Team or Enterprise login where the transcript gets notices that a workmap hook was skipped. The map then loses the Hooks station, the records a hook adds, the row of a typed slash command and the mark of a compaction; everything else stays.

theme.title: Colours
theme.description: The map's colours: dark, light, contrast (the dark ones at full contrast, on black), or auto, which is dark on a dark surface and light on a light one.

background.title: Background
background.description: The map's own background, or transparent, which lets the pane behind it show through.

colors.title: Colours of your own
colors.description: Colours that replace the map's own, each written as name=#rrggbb. Names: background, node, line, spoke, text, label, faint, accent, active, error, memory, memoryActive, route. Set theme to dark or light with them.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: With reduced, nothing on the map moves by itself: no pulses, rings, beams, blinking or spinning, and the cells repaint slowly. The same state is shown still.

terminalMap.title: Map in a terminal
terminalMap.description: In a terminal, draw the map in coloured cells above the rows. Off, a terminal shows the rows and one line of counts.

terminalPicture.title: Pictures in a terminal
terminalPicture.description: In a terminal that shows pictures such as kitty or Ghostty, but not iTerm2, which keeps every frame in memory, auto has a headless Chromium paint the map as the app draws it, and the pane shows each frame. It needs Node and Chromium; without them, and with off, the map stays in cells.

terminalWindow.title: Map window in Windows Terminal
terminalWindow.description: In Windows Terminal from WSL, auto makes the map a window of its own in place of the pane: an Edge app window you can drag, resize and move to another screen, with the rows under it and tooltips over it, opened the first time you write in the session. Pane splits the terminal's tab for the map instead, as a picture; off keeps the pane, in cells.

notify.title: Notify when Claude needs you
notify.description: Raise a notification when Claude asks you a question or puts a plan to you, when a permission prompt has waited on you for a second (naming the call, as its row does), and when a turn ends. Useful for sessions running in the background.

windowRows.title: Rows under the map in its window
windowRows.description: The rows the map window keeps for the list under the map (the action now, Claude's plan, background work, the calls), from 3 to 30. The map takes the rest, as large as the window's width allows, and never fewer than 12 rows.

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: Where you are on the map: at the top, or at the bottom with the network and the browser at the top.

spokes.title: Spokes wear by
spokes.description: What thickens a station's spoke: the calls it took (calls), or its share of the time Claude spent on calls (time), so one slow call weighs more than many quick ones.
